title.tet: Ema dahuluk iha Timór (maizumenus tinan 44 000 liubá)
title.pt: Os primeiros povos (há cerca de 44 000 anos)
title.en: The first peoples (about 44,000 years ago)

summary.tet: Ema hela iha Timór maizumenus tinan 44 000 ona. Sira mai ho ró liu tasi, hela iha fatuk-kuak no kaer ikan iha tasi kle'an. Ohin loron arkeólogu sira hetan sira-nia ekipamentu, ikan nia ruin no pintura iha fatuk-kuak hanesan Laili, Jerimalai no Lene Hara.
summary.pt: Há pessoas a viver em Timor há cerca de 44 000 anos. Chegaram de barco, viviam em grutas e pescavam em alto mar. As suas ferramentas, ossos de peixe e pinturas ainda se encontram em grutas como Laili, Jerimalai e Lene Hara.
summary.id: Manusia sudah tinggal di Timor sekitar 44.000 tahun. Mereka datang dengan perahu, tinggal di gua dan menangkap ikan di laut dalam. Alat, tulang ikan dan lukisan mereka masih ditemukan di gua seperti Laili, Jerimalai dan Lene Hara.
summary.en: People have lived on Timor for about 44,000 years. They came by boat, lived in caves and caught fish in the deep sea. Their tools, fish bones and paintings are still found in caves such as Laili, Jerimalai and Lene Hara.

text.tet: Timór iha Wallacea, zona illa sira entre Ázia no Austrália. Tasi kle'an fahe nafatin illa ne'e husi rai-kontinente Ázia, maski iha tempu jelu, bainhira tasi nia nível tun liu ohin loron. Tan ne'e, ema dahuluk ne'ebé to'o Timór tenke uza ró ka rakit. Sira mak ema modernu (Homo sapiens). Sira-nia bei'ala sai husi Áfrika tinan rihun barak uluk. Arkeólogu sira estuda buat ne'ebé ema sira-ne'e husik hela: ekipamentu fatuk, kulit-tasi, animál no ikan nia ruin, okre (rai-mean) no ahi nia rastu. Bainhira sira sukat buat sira-ne'e nia idade, sira hatene bainhira ema hela iha fatuk-kuak ida-idak.
text.pt: Timor fica na Wallacea, uma zona de ilhas entre a Ásia e a Austrália. O mar profundo sempre a separou do continente asiático, mesmo nas eras glaciares, quando o nível do mar era muito mais baixo do que hoje. Por isso, os primeiros humanos que chegaram a Timor tiveram de usar barcos ou jangadas. Eram humanos modernos (Homo sapiens), cujos antepassados tinham saído de África dezenas de milhares de anos antes. Os arqueólogos estudam o que essas pessoas deixaram: ferramentas de pedra, conchas, ossos de animais e de peixes, ocre e cinzas de fogueiras. Ao datar estes restos, sabem quando houve gente em cada gruta.
text.id: Timor terletak di Wallacea, kawasan pulau-pulau di antara Asia dan Australia. Laut dalam selalu memisahkannya dari daratan Asia, bahkan pada zaman es, ketika permukaan laut jauh lebih rendah daripada sekarang. Karena itu, manusia pertama yang tiba di Timor pasti memakai perahu atau rakit. Mereka adalah manusia modern (Homo sapiens), yang leluhurnya meninggalkan Afrika puluhan ribu tahun sebelumnya. Arkeolog mempelajari apa yang mereka tinggalkan: alat batu, cangkang kerang, tulang hewan dan ikan, oker, serta abu bekas api. Dengan menentukan umur sisa-sisa itu, arkeolog dapat mengetahui kapan manusia tinggal di setiap gua.
text.en: Timor lies in Wallacea, a zone of islands between Asia and Australia. Deep sea has always separated it from the Asian mainland, even in the ice ages, when the sea level was much lower than today. So the first people who reached Timor must have used boats or rafts. They were modern humans (Homo sapiens), whose ancestors had left Africa tens of thousands of years earlier. Archaeologists study what these people left behind: stone tools, shells, animal and fish bones, ochre and the ash of old fires. By dating these remains, they can tell when people lived in each cave.

text.tet: Laili mak fatuk-kuak ki'ik ida iha munisípiu Manatutu, iha parte norte. Iha tinan 2024, ekipa arkeólogu husi University College London no universidade sira iha Austrália publika estudu ida iha revista Nature Communications. Sira sukat rai-kamada nia idade ho métodu ida ne'ebé hatene bainhira rai-henek nia fuan sira hetan naroman loron ikus liu. Rai-kamada husi tinan 59 000 to'o 54 000 liubá la hatudu ema nia rastu ne'ebé klaru. Depois, maizumenus tinan 44 000 liubá, ekipamentu fatuk barak no ema nia rastu seluk mosu. Ekipa ne'e hanaran ida-ne'e 'sinál to'o mai' ema dahuluk nian. Ne'e hatudu katak ema to'o Timór tarde liu duké sientista balu hanoin uluk.
text.pt: Laili é um abrigo rochoso no município de Manatuto, no norte do país. Em 2024, uma equipa de arqueólogos da University College London e de universidades australianas publicou um estudo na revista Nature Communications. Os investigadores dataram as camadas de sedimento com um método que mede quando os grãos de areia foram expostos à luz do sol pela última vez. As camadas de há cerca de 59 000 a 54 000 anos não mostram sinais claros de presença humana. Depois, há cerca de 44 000 anos, aparecem muitas ferramentas de pedra e outros vestígios. A equipa chamou-lhe a 'assinatura de chegada' dos primeiros humanos. O estudo sugere que as pessoas chegaram mais tarde do que alguns cientistas pensavam.
text.id: Laili adalah ceruk batu di Manatuto, di bagian utara negara itu. Pada 2024, tim arkeolog dari University College London dan universitas-universitas Australia menerbitkan penelitian di jurnal Nature Communications. Mereka menentukan umur lapisan tanah dengan metode yang mengukur kapan butir pasir terakhir kali terkena sinar matahari. Lapisan dari sekitar 59.000 hingga 54.000 tahun lalu tidak menunjukkan tanda manusia yang jelas. Lalu, sekitar 44.000 tahun lalu, banyak alat batu dan jejak manusia lain muncul. Tim itu menyebutnya 'tanda kedatangan' manusia pertama. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa manusia tiba di Timor lebih lambat daripada perkiraan sebagian ilmuwan.
text.en: Laili is a rock shelter in Manatuto municipality, in the north of the country. In 2024 a team of archaeologists from University College London and Australian universities published a study in the journal Nature Communications. They dated the layers of soil with a method that measures when grains of sand were last exposed to sunlight. Layers from about 59,000 to 54,000 years ago showed no clear sign of people. Then, about 44,000 years ago, many stone tools and other traces of people appear. The team called this the 'arrival signature' of the first humans. It suggests that people reached Timor later than some scientists had thought.

heading.tet: Jerimalai: kaer ikan iha tasi kle'an
heading.id: Jerimalai: menangkap ikan di laut dalam
heading.en: Jerimalai: fishing in the deep sea

text.tet: Jerimalai mak fatuk-kuak ki'ik ida husi fatuk-ahu, besik Tutuala, iha Timór-Leste nia rohan loro-sa'e, munisípiu Lautein. Iha tinan 2011, ekipa ida ne'ebé Sue O'Connor husi Universidade Nasionál Austrália lidera, fó-sai iha revista Science katak ema iha ne'ebá kaer ikan ona maizumenus tinan 42 000 liubá. Fatin ne'e iha ikan nia ruin liu 38 000, husi ikan maizumenus 2 800. Maizumenus metade mai husi ikan tasi kle'an ne'ebé nani lalais, hanesan atun. Atu kaer ikan sira-ne'e, ema presiza ró, planu no matenek. Ekipa ne'e mós hetan anzól nia pedasuk husi kulit-tasi, ho idade maizumenus tinan 23 000 to'o 16 000. Ida-ne'e anzól tuan liu ida iha mundu.
text.pt: Jerimalai é um abrigo rochoso de calcário perto de Tutuala, no extremo leste do país, em Lautém. Em 2011, uma equipa dirigida por Sue O'Connor, da Universidade Nacional Australiana, publicou na revista Science que ali se pescava há cerca de 42 000 anos. O sítio tinha mais de 38 000 ossos de peixe, de cerca de 2800 peixes. Cerca de metade vinha de peixes rápidos do alto mar, como o atum. Para os apanhar eram precisos barcos, planeamento e muita habilidade. A equipa encontrou também fragmentos de um anzol feito de concha, com cerca de 23 000 a 16 000 anos, um dos mais antigos conhecidos no mundo.
text.id: Jerimalai adalah ceruk batu kapur di dekat Tutuala, di ujung timur negara ini, di Lautém. Pada 2011, tim yang dipimpin Sue O'Connor dari Universitas Nasional Australia melaporkan di jurnal Science bahwa orang di sana sudah menangkap ikan sekitar 42.000 tahun lalu. Situs itu menyimpan lebih dari 38.000 tulang ikan dari sekitar 2.800 ekor ikan. Sekitar separuhnya berasal dari ikan laut lepas yang cepat, seperti tuna. Untuk menangkapnya diperlukan perahu, perencanaan dan keterampilan. Tim itu juga menemukan pecahan kail dari cangkang kerang yang berumur sekitar 23.000 hingga 16.000 tahun, salah satu kail tertua yang diketahui di dunia.
text.en: Jerimalai is a limestone rock shelter near Tutuala, at the eastern tip of the country, in Lautém. In 2011 a team led by Sue O'Connor of the Australian National University reported in the journal Science that people there caught fish about 42,000 years ago. The site held more than 38,000 fish bones from about 2,800 fish. About half came from fast fish of the open sea, such as tuna. Catching them needs boats, planning and skill. The team also found pieces of a fish hook made of shell, about 23,000 to 16,000 years old, one of the oldest known in the world.

heading.tet: Lene Hara: pintura no oin ema iha fatuk
heading.pt: Lene Hara: pinturas e rostos na rocha
heading.id: Lene Hara: lukisan dan wajah di batu
heading.en: Lene Hara: rock art and carved faces

text.tet: Lene Hara mak fatuk-kuak boot ida iha área Tutuala, iha Parke Nasionál Nino Konis Santana nia laran. Ema uza ona fatuk-kuak ne'e tinan rihun barak liubá: fatuk-ahu pedasuk ida ho okre mean iha idade liu tinan 30 000. Fatuk-kuak sira iha área ne'e iha pintura mean ho ema, ró no animál. Iha Lene Hara, sientista sira uza métodu urániu atu sukat kamada minerál ki'ik sira. Pintura ne'ebé ita haree ohin nia idade menus husi maizumenus tinan 6 300, maibé kór mean tuan ida iha okos iha idade maizumenus tinan 24 000 to'o 29 000. Iha tinan 2010, sientista sira fó-sai mós ema nia oin ne'ebé ema ko'a iha fatuk, ho idade maizumenus tinan 10 000 to'o 12 000. Fatuk-kuak barak iha Lautein lulik ba komunidade Fataluku.
text.pt: Lene Hara é uma grande gruta na zona de Tutuala, dentro do atual Parque Nacional Nino Konis Santana. Já era usada há dezenas de milhares de anos: um fragmento de calcário com ocre vermelho tem mais de 30 000 anos. As grutas desta zona têm pinturas vermelhas de pessoas, barcos e animais. Em Lene Hara, a datação por urânio de finas crostas minerais mostrou que as pinturas visíveis têm menos de cerca de 6300 anos, mas uma camada mais antiga de pigmento vermelho tem entre 24 000 e 29 000 anos. Em 2010, cientistas descreveram também rostos humanos gravados na rocha, com cerca de 10 000 a 12 000 anos. Muitas grutas de Lautém são sagradas para as comunidades fataluku.
text.id: Lene Hara adalah gua besar di wilayah Tutuala, di dalam Taman Nasional Nino Konis Santana sekarang. Gua ini sudah dipakai puluhan ribu tahun lalu: sepotong batu kapur dengan oker merah berumur lebih dari 30.000 tahun. Gua-gua di wilayah ini memiliki lukisan merah berupa manusia, perahu dan hewan. Di Lene Hara, penanggalan uranium pada kerak mineral tipis menunjukkan bahwa lukisan yang terlihat berumur kurang dari sekitar 6.300 tahun, tetapi lapisan pigmen merah yang lebih tua berumur sekitar 24.000 sampai 29.000 tahun. Pada 2010, ilmuwan juga melaporkan wajah manusia yang dipahat di batu, berumur sekitar 10.000 sampai 12.000 tahun. Banyak gua di Lautém sakral bagi masyarakat Fataluku.
text.en: Lene Hara is a large cave in the Tutuala area, inside today's Nino Konis Santana National Park. People used it tens of thousands of years ago: a piece of limestone with red ochre is more than 30,000 years old. Caves in this area have red paintings of people, boats and animals. At Lene Hara, uranium-series dating of thin mineral crusts showed that the visible paintings are younger than about 6,300 years, but an older layer of red pigment is about 24,000 to 29,000 years old. In 2010 scientists also reported human faces carved into the rock, about 10,000 to 12,000 years old. Many caves in Lautém are sacred to Fataluku communities.

title.tet: Povu Austronéziu no Papua
title.pt: Povos austronésios e papuas
title.en: Austronesian and Papuan peoples

summary.tet: Povu Timór-Leste nian ko'alia lian husi família boot rua: Austronézia no Papua. Ema ne'ebé ko'alia lian Austronézia mai liu tasi tinan rihun hirak liubá, no lori sanan-rai no to'os. Durante tinan rihun barak grupu sira hasoru malu, kahur malu no harii kultura ohin loron nian.
summary.pt: Os povos de Timor-Leste falam línguas de duas grandes famílias: austronésia e papua. Os falantes de línguas austronésias chegaram por mar há alguns milhares de anos e trouxeram a cerâmica e a agricultura. Ao longo de milhares de anos, os grupos encontraram-se, misturaram-se e formaram as culturas de hoje.
summary.id: Penduduk Timor-Leste berbicara bahasa dari dua rumpun besar: Austronesia dan Papua. Penutur bahasa Austronesia datang lewat laut beberapa ribu tahun lalu dan membawa tembikar serta pertanian. Selama ribuan tahun kelompok-kelompok ini bertemu, berbaur dan membentuk budaya masa kini.
summary.en: Timor-Leste's peoples speak languages from two big families: Austronesian and Papuan. Austronesian speakers came by sea a few thousand years ago and brought pottery and farming. Over thousands of years the groups met, mixed and shaped the cultures of today.

text.tet: Linguista sira (espesialista lian nian) fahe Timór-Leste nia lian sira ba família rua. Lian barak liu mak parte husi família Austronézia. Família ne'e luan tebes, husi Taiwan no Filipinas to'o Indonézia, illa sira iha Pasífiku no Madagaskar. Tetun, Mambai, Kemak, Tokodede, Galoli, Baikeno no Waima'a mak lian Austronézia. Grupu ki'ik liu ida, ne'ebé ema bolu Papua ka la'ós Austronézia, parte husi família Timór-Alor-Pantar. Iha Timór-Leste, lian sira-ne'e mak Fataluku, Makasae, Makalero no Bunak. Linguista balu hanoin katak família ne'e iha relasaun dook ho lian sira iha Nova Giné. Família rua ne'e hela besik malu iha Timór durante tinan 3 000 ka liu.
text.pt: Os linguistas agrupam as línguas de Timor-Leste em duas famílias. A maioria pertence à família austronésia, espalhada de Taiwan e das Filipinas até à Indonésia, às ilhas do Pacífico e a Madagáscar. Tétum, mambai, kemak, tokodede, galoli, baikeno e waima'a são línguas austronésias. Um grupo menor, chamado papua ou não austronésio, pertence à família Timor-Alor-Pantar. Em Timor-Leste, são o fataluku, o makasae, o makalero e o bunak. Alguns linguistas pensam que esta família tem um parentesco distante com línguas da Nova Guiné. As duas famílias vivem lado a lado em Timor há pelo menos 3000 anos.
text.id: Para ahli bahasa membagi bahasa-bahasa di Timor-Leste ke dalam dua rumpun. Sebagian besar termasuk rumpun Austronesia, yang tersebar dari Taiwan dan Filipina sampai Indonesia, kepulauan Pasifik dan Madagaskar. Tetun, Mambai, Kemak, Tokodede, Galoli, Baikeno dan Waima'a adalah bahasa Austronesia. Kelompok yang lebih kecil, yang disebut Papua atau non-Austronesia, termasuk rumpun Timor-Alor-Pantar. Di Timor-Leste, bahasa-bahasa ini adalah Fataluku, Makasae, Makalero dan Bunak. Sebagian ahli bahasa menduga rumpun ini berkerabat jauh dengan bahasa-bahasa di Nugini. Kedua rumpun sudah hidup berdampingan di Timor sedikitnya 3.000 tahun.
text.en: Linguists group the languages of Timor-Leste into two families. Most belong to the Austronesian family, which stretches from Taiwan and the Philippines to Indonesia, the Pacific islands and Madagascar. Tetun, Mambai, Kemak, Tokodede, Galoli, Baikeno and Waima'a are Austronesian. A smaller group, called Papuan or non-Austronesian, belongs to the Timor-Alor-Pantar family. In Timor-Leste these are Fataluku, Makasae, Makalero and Bunak. Some linguists think this family is distantly related to languages of New Guinea. The two families have lived side by side on Timor for at least 3,000 years.

text.tet: Povu sira ne'ebé ko'alia lian Austronézia namkari liu tasi ba Ázia Sudeste nia illa sira. Sira hahú husi Taiwan tinan rihun hirak liubá. Arkeólogu sira hanoin katak sira to'o Timór entre tinan 4 500 no 3 000 liubá; fonte sira fó data la hanesan. Sira la'o ho ró, no lori moris foun: sanan-rai, kuda ai-horis ba hahán no hakiak animál. Iha Timór-Leste, sanan-rai mosu iha fatuk-kuak sira tinan 3 500 liubá ka uluk liu. To'os muda neineik ema nia moris: ema ko'a ai-laran atu halo to'os, no knua sira sai boot. Lian sira hatudu relasaun ne'e: liafuan Tetun 'lima' no 'mata' hanesan ho 'lima' no 'mata' iha lian Malaiu no Tagalog.
text.pt: Os povos de língua austronésia espalharam-se por mar pelas ilhas do Sudeste Asiático, partindo de Taiwan há alguns milhares de anos. Os arqueólogos pensam que chegaram a Timor entre há cerca de 4500 e 3000 anos; as fontes dão datas diferentes. Navegavam em canoas e trouxeram novos modos de vida: a cerâmica, o cultivo de plantas e os animais domésticos. Em Timor-Leste, a cerâmica aparece nas grutas há pelo menos 3500 anos. A agricultura mudou a vida devagar: as pessoas abriam clareiras na floresta para hortas e as aldeias cresceram. As línguas mostram este parentesco: as palavras tétum 'lima' (cinco) e 'mata' (olho) são iguais às do malaio e do tagalo.
text.id: Bangsa penutur bahasa Austronesia menyebar lewat laut ke pulau-pulau Asia Tenggara, berangkat dari Taiwan beberapa ribu tahun lalu. Arkeolog menduga mereka tiba di Timor antara sekitar 4.500 dan 3.000 tahun lalu; sumber-sumber memberi tanggal yang berbeda. Mereka berlayar dengan perahu dan membawa cara hidup baru: tembikar, menanam tanaman pangan dan memelihara hewan. Di Timor-Leste, tembikar muncul di gua-gua sedikitnya 3.500 tahun lalu. Pertanian perlahan mengubah kehidupan: orang membuka hutan untuk kebun, dan kampung-kampung tumbuh. Bahasa menunjukkan hubungan ini: kata Tetun 'lima' (lima) dan 'mata' (mata) sama dengan kata dalam bahasa Melayu dan Tagalog.
text.en: Austronesian-speaking peoples spread by sea across the islands of Southeast Asia, starting from Taiwan several thousand years ago. Archaeologists think they reached Timor between about 4,500 and 3,000 years ago; sources give different dates. They sailed in canoes and brought new ways of life: pottery, growing food crops and keeping domestic animals. In Timor-Leste, pottery appears in caves at least 3,500 years ago. Farming slowly changed life: people cleared forest for gardens, and villages grew. Languages show this link: the Tetun words 'lima' (five) and 'mata' (eye) are the same as in Malay and Tagalog.

heading.tet: Povu sira ne'ebé ko'alia lian Papua

text.tet: Ema ko'alia lian Papua iha Timór-Leste liuliu iha parte loro-sa'e no iha klaran. Fataluku mak lian iha Lautein, iha Lospalos no Tutuala. Makasae iha Baukau no Vikeke, no Makalero iha área Iliomar. Bunak iha foho sira Bobonaru no Kovalima nian, no mós iha fronteira nia sorin seluk, iha Timór loro-monu (Indonézia). Peskizadór sira sei diskute bainhira no oinsá ema sira-ne'e nia bei'ala to'o mai. Hanoin ida mak sira mai husi área Nova Giné. Ho tempu, lian Papua sira foti liafuan barak husi sira-nia viziñu Austronézia, no sira fahe lisan barak hamutuk.
text.pt: As línguas papuas de Timor-Leste falam-se sobretudo no leste e no centro. O fataluku fala-se em Lautém, em Lospalos e Tutuala. O makasae fala-se em Baucau e Viqueque, e o makalero na zona de Iliomar. O bunak fala-se nas montanhas de Bobonaro e Cova Lima e também do outro lado da fronteira, em Timor Ocidental. Os investigadores ainda discutem quando e como chegaram os antepassados destes falantes; uma hipótese é que vieram da região da Nova Guiné. Com o tempo, estas línguas adotaram muitas palavras dos vizinhos austronésios, e os seus falantes partilham com eles muitos costumes.
text.id: Bahasa-bahasa Papua di Timor-Leste dituturkan terutama di bagian timur dan tengah. Fataluku dituturkan di Lautém, di sekitar Lospalos dan Tutuala. Makasae dituturkan di Baucau dan Viqueque, dan Makalero di daerah Iliomar. Bunak dituturkan di pegunungan Bobonaro dan Cova Lima, juga di seberang perbatasan, di Timor Barat. Para peneliti masih memperdebatkan kapan dan bagaimana leluhur para penuturnya datang; salah satu dugaan menyebut mereka berasal dari wilayah Nugini. Seiring waktu, bahasa-bahasa ini meminjam banyak kata dari tetangga Austronesia, dan penuturnya berbagi banyak adat dengan mereka.
text.en: The Papuan languages of Timor-Leste are spoken mainly in the east and in the centre. Fataluku is spoken in Lautém, around Lospalos and Tutuala. Makasae is spoken in Baucau and Viqueque, and Makalero in the Iliomar area. Bunak is spoken in the mountains of Bobonaro and Covalima and across the border in West Timor. Researchers still debate when and how the ancestors of these speakers came; one idea is that they came from the New Guinea area. Over time these languages borrowed many words from their Austronesian neighbours, and their speakers share many customs with them.

heading.tet: Kahur malu no lian sira ohin loron
heading.pt: Mistura e as línguas de hoje
heading.en: Mixing and the languages of today

text.tet: Durante tinan rihun barak, grupu Austronézia no Papua halo negósiu, kaben malu, funu no halo aliansa. Ema nia raan, liafuan no lisan hatudu kahur naruk ida-ne'e. Tan ne'e, família lian la hatudu ema nia 'rasa' ka orijen. Timór-oan barak ko'alia lian barak: sira-nia lian-inan, Tetun, no dala barak Portugés, Indonézia ka Inglés. Lian ki'ik balu iha perigu atu lakon. Iha sensu 2010, lian Makuva iha Lautein iha ema na'in 56 de'it ne'ebé ko'alia. Konstituisaun hatuur Tetun no Portugés nu'udar lian ofisiál, no hateten katak Estadu valoriza no dezenvolve Tetun no lian nasionál sira seluk.
text.pt: Durante milhares de anos, grupos austronésios e papuas fizeram comércio, casaram entre si, combateram e fizeram alianças. Os genes, as palavras e os costumes mostram esta longa mistura; por isso, a família de uma língua não indica a 'raça' ou a origem de quem a fala. Muitos timorenses falam várias línguas: a língua materna, o tétum e, muitas vezes, português, indonésio ou inglês. Algumas línguas pequenas estão em perigo: no censo de 2010, o makuva, em Lautém, tinha só 56 falantes. A Constituição faz do tétum e do português as línguas oficiais e diz que o Estado valoriza e desenvolve o tétum e as outras línguas nacionais.
text.id: Selama ribuan tahun, kelompok Austronesia dan Papua berdagang, saling menikah, berperang dan membuat persekutuan. Gen, kata dan adat menunjukkan percampuran panjang ini, sehingga rumpun bahasa tidak menunjukkan 'ras' atau asal-usul penuturnya. Banyak orang Timor berbicara beberapa bahasa: bahasa ibu, Tetun, dan sering juga Portugis, Indonesia atau Inggris. Beberapa bahasa kecil terancam punah: dalam sensus 2010, bahasa Makuva di Lautém hanya memiliki 56 penutur. Konstitusi menetapkan Tetun dan Portugis sebagai bahasa resmi dan menyatakan bahwa negara menghargai serta mengembangkan Tetun dan bahasa nasional lainnya.
text.en: Over thousands of years, Austronesian and Papuan groups traded, married, fought and made alliances. Genes, words and customs show this long mixing, so a language family does not tell the 'race' or origin of its speakers. Many Timorese speak several languages: their mother tongue, Tetun and often Portuguese, Indonesian or English. Some small languages are in danger: in the 2010 census, Makuva, in Lautém, had only 56 speakers. The Constitution makes Tetun and Portuguese the official languages and says that the State values and develops Tetun and the other national languages.

summary.pt: Antes e durante o domínio português, Timor estava dividido em muitos pequenos reinos. Cada reino era chefiado por um liurai, um governante ligado às casas sagradas e aos antepassados. O reino de Wehali, na costa sul, era honrado por muitos outros como centro ritual.
summary.id: Sebelum dan selama kekuasaan Portugis, Timor terbagi menjadi banyak kerajaan kecil. Setiap kerajaan dipimpin seorang liurai, penguasa yang terkait dengan rumah adat dan para leluhur. Kerajaan Wehali di pantai selatan dihormati banyak kerajaan lain sebagai pusat ritual.
summary.en: Before and during Portuguese rule, Timor was divided into many small kingdoms. Each was led by a liurai, a ruler linked to sacred houses and ancestors. The kingdom of Wehali, on the south coast, was honoured by many others as a ritual centre.

text.tet: Molok ema Europa mai, Timór nunka hamutuk iha ukun-na'in ida nia okos. Illa ne'e iha reinu ki'ik barak. Iha Tetun, liurai ida nia rai ema bolu 'rai', no Portugés sira bolu rai sira-ne'e 'reino' (reinu). Reinu ida-idak iha suku no knua sira, ne'ebé dato no katuas sira lidera. Ligasaun família, uma lulik no lisan mak kesi reinu ida hamutuk. Reinu sira halo aliansa liuhusi kazamentu no juramentu lulik, troka prezente, no dala ruma funu malu tanba rai, bee no negósiu. Reinu tuan barak husik hela sira-nia naran ba fatin ne'ebé ita koñese ohin loron.
text.pt: Antes da chegada dos europeus, Timor nunca esteve unido sob um só governante. A ilha estava dividida em muitos pequenos reinos. Em tétum, a terra de um governante chamava-se rai, e os portugueses chamaram reinos a estas terras. Cada reino tinha sucos e povoações, chefiados por nobres e anciãos, e mantinha-se unido por laços de família, casas sagradas (uma lulik) e pelo direito costumeiro (lisan). Os reinos faziam alianças através de casamentos e juramentos rituais, trocavam presentes e, por vezes, combatiam entre si por terra, água e comércio. Muitos destes reinos antigos deram o nome a lugares que hoje conhecemos.
text.id: Sebelum orang Eropa datang, Timor tidak pernah bersatu di bawah satu penguasa. Pulau ini terdiri atas banyak kerajaan kecil. Dalam bahasa Tetun, wilayah seorang penguasa disebut rai, dan orang Portugis menyebut wilayah-wilayah itu reino, artinya kerajaan. Setiap kerajaan memiliki desa dan kampung yang dipimpin bangsawan dan para tetua, dan disatukan oleh ikatan keluarga, rumah adat (uma lulik) serta hukum adat (lisan). Kerajaan-kerajaan membuat persekutuan melalui perkawinan dan sumpah adat, saling bertukar hadiah, dan kadang berperang memperebutkan tanah, air dan perdagangan. Banyak kerajaan lama mewariskan namanya pada tempat yang kita kenal sekarang.
text.en: Before the Europeans came, Timor was never united under one ruler. The island was made up of many small kingdoms. In Tetun a ruler's land was called rai, and the Portuguese called these lands reinos, meaning kingdoms. Each kingdom had villages and hamlets led by nobles and elders, and it was held together by family ties, sacred houses (uma lulik) and customary law (lisan). Kingdoms made alliances through marriages and ritual oaths, exchanged gifts, and sometimes fought each other over land, water and trade. Many of these old kingdoms gave their names to places we know today.

text.tet: Ema bolu ukun-na'in reinu nian 'liurai'. Ema dala barak esplika liafuan ne'e hanesan 'liu rai' (liu = liu ba leten, rai = rai). Liurai lidera funu, rezolve problema no fahe rai, maibé nia la ukun mesak. Na'i-lulik sira, dato sira no katuas uma lulik nian mós iha podér boot. Portugés sira ukun durante sékulu barak liuhusi liurai sira, no fó sira títulu hanesan 'Dom' no grau militár. Depois funu 1911–1912, reinu sira lakon sira-nia podér barak. Maski nune'e, família liurai barak sei hetan respeitu, no reinu sira moris nafatin hanesan rai lulik.
text.pt: O governante de um reino chamava-se liurai, palavra tétum muitas vezes explicada como 'acima da terra' (liu = além, rai = terra). O liurai comandava na guerra, resolvia disputas e repartia a terra, mas não governava sozinho: os sacerdotes rituais, os nobres chamados dato e os anciãos das casas sagradas também tinham grande autoridade. Durante séculos, os portugueses governaram através dos liurais, dando-lhes títulos como 'Dom' e postos militares. Depois da guerra de 1911–1912, os reinos perderam a maior parte do seu poder, mas muitas famílias de liurais continuam respeitadas e os reinos sobrevivem como domínios rituais.
text.id: Penguasa sebuah kerajaan disebut liurai, kata Tetun yang sering dijelaskan sebagai 'melampaui bumi' (liu = melampaui, rai = bumi atau tanah). Liurai memimpin perang, menyelesaikan sengketa dan membagi tanah, tetapi ia tidak memerintah sendirian: pemuka ritual, bangsawan yang disebut dato, dan para tetua rumah adat juga sangat berwibawa. Selama berabad-abad Portugis memerintah melalui para liurai dan memberi mereka gelar seperti 'Dom' serta pangkat militer. Setelah perang 1911–1912, kerajaan-kerajaan kehilangan sebagian besar kekuasaannya, tetapi banyak keluarga liurai tetap dihormati, dan kerajaan-kerajaan itu bertahan sebagai wilayah adat.
text.en: The ruler of a kingdom was called liurai, a Tetun word often explained as 'surpassing the earth' (liu = beyond, rai = earth or land). The liurai led in war, settled disputes and shared out land, but he did not rule alone: ritual leaders, nobles called dato and the elders of the sacred houses also had great authority. For centuries the Portuguese ruled through the liurai, giving them titles such as 'Dom' and military ranks. After the war of 1911–1912 the kingdoms lost most of their power, but many liurai families are still respected, and the kingdoms live on as ritual domains.

text.tet: Iha Timór klaran nia tasi-ibun sul iha Wehali, naran seluk Wewiku-Wehali, iha rai Belu ne'ebé ko'alia Tetun (ohin loron iha Indonézia). Istória barak husi Timór dehan katak Wehali mak rai dahuluk ne'ebé sa'e husi tasi. Ninia ema aas liu mak Maromak Oan, 'Maromak nia oan'. Nia hela nonok hanesan fatin lulik nia klaran, no liurai ida ukun iha ninia naran. Reinu barak iha illa tomak fó onra ba Wehali hanesan sira-nia maun-boot. Atake Portugés iha 1642 no 1665 halo Wehali nia podér sai fraku. Bainhira sira hatuur fronteira iha 1859, Wehali nia sentru tama iha Olanda nia parte.
text.pt: Na costa sul do centro de Timor ficava Wehali, também chamado Wewiku-Wehali, na terra de língua tétum de Belu (hoje na Indonésia). Muitas histórias timorenses contam que Wehali foi a primeira terra a sair do mar. A sua figura mais alta era o Maromak Oan, 'filho de Deus', que permanecia quieto como um centro sagrado, enquanto um liurai governava em seu nome. Muitos reinos da ilha honravam Wehali como o seu irmão mais velho. Ataques portugueses em 1642 e 1665 enfraqueceram o seu poder. Quando a fronteira foi traçada, em 1859, o centro de Wehali ficou do lado holandês.
text.id: Di pantai selatan Timor bagian tengah terletak Wehali, juga disebut Wewiku-Wehali, di tanah Belu yang berbahasa Tetun (kini di Indonesia). Banyak cerita Timor mengatakan bahwa Wehali adalah daratan pertama yang muncul dari laut. Tokoh tertingginya adalah Maromak Oan, 'putra Tuhan', yang diam tenang sebagai pusat suci, sementara seorang liurai memerintah atas namanya. Banyak kerajaan di seluruh pulau menghormati Wehali sebagai saudara tertua. Serangan Portugis pada 1642 dan 1665 melemahkan kekuasaannya. Ketika perbatasan ditetapkan pada 1859, pusat Wehali masuk ke wilayah Belanda.
text.en: On the south coast of central Timor lay Wehali, also called Wewiku-Wehali, in the Tetun-speaking land of Belu (today in Indonesia). Many Timorese stories say that Wehali was the first land to rise from the sea. Its highest figure was the Maromak Oan, 'son of God', who stayed still like a sacred centre, while a liurai governed in his name. Many kingdoms across the island honoured Wehali as their elder brother. Portuguese attacks in 1642 and 1665 weakened its power. When the border was settled in 1859, Wehali's centre fell on the Dutch side.

text.tet: Eskritór Portugés sira iha sékulu 17 no 18 fahe Timór ba 'provínsia' rua. Servião iha loro-monu mak povu Atoni (Dawan) nia rai, ho reinu maizumenus 16. Belos ka Belu iha klaran no loro-sa'e iha reinu barak liu: lista tuan sira temi maizumenus 46 to'o 50. Istoriadór sira, hanesan Hans Hägerdal, dehan katak divizaun ne'e mak ideia koloniál: ninia liña sira muda, no la hanesan loloos ho fronteira Olanda no Portugés nian depois. Ikus mai, Servião nia parte barak liu tama Olanda nia okos, no Belos nia parte barak liu tama Portugés nia okos.
text.pt: Os escritores portugueses dos séculos XVII e XVIII dividiam Timor em duas 'províncias'. O Servião, a oeste, era a terra do povo atoni (dawan), com cerca de 16 reinos. Belos, ou Belu, no centro e no leste, tinha muitos mais reinos: as listas antigas falam de cerca de 46 a 50. Historiadores como Hans Hägerdal lembram que esta divisão era uma ideia colonial: os limites mudavam e não coincidiam exatamente com as fronteiras holandesas e portuguesas posteriores. No fim, a maior parte do Servião ficou sob os holandeses e a maior parte de Belos sob os portugueses.
text.id: Para penulis Portugis abad ke-17 dan ke-18 membagi Timor menjadi dua 'provinsi'. Servião di barat adalah tanah orang Atoni (Dawan), dengan sekitar 16 kerajaan. Belos atau Belu, di tengah dan timur, memiliki jauh lebih banyak kerajaan: daftar-daftar lama menyebut sekitar 46 sampai 50. Sejarawan seperti Hans Hägerdal mengingatkan bahwa pembagian ini adalah gagasan kolonial: batasnya berubah-ubah dan tidak persis sama dengan perbatasan Belanda dan Portugis kemudian. Akhirnya, sebagian besar Servião jatuh ke tangan Belanda dan sebagian besar Belos ke tangan Portugis.
text.en: Portuguese writers of the 17th and 18th centuries divided Timor into two 'provinces'. Servião, in the west, was the land of the Atoni (Dawan) people, with about 16 kingdoms. Belos, or Belu, in the centre and east, had many more kingdoms: old lists give about 46 to 50. Historians such as Hans Hägerdal point out that this division was a colonial idea: its limits moved, and they did not match the later Dutch and Portuguese borders exactly. In the end, most of Servião came under the Dutch and most of Belos under the Portuguese.

title.pt: O comércio do sândalo
title.en: The sandalwood trade

summary.tet: Durante sékulu barak Timór famozu ho ai-kameli mutin, ai morin ida ne'ebé ema iha Xina, Índia no fatin seluk hakarak tebes. Komersiante Xina, Java, Malaiu no depois Europa nian mai Timór atu sosa. Negósiu ne'e lori riku-soin ba reinu sira, maibé mós funu, no iha sékulu 19 ai-kameli fuik sai menus tebes ona.
summary.pt: Durante séculos, Timor foi famoso pelo sândalo branco, uma madeira perfumada muito procurada na China, na Índia e noutros lugares. Mercadores chineses, javaneses, malaios e, mais tarde, europeus navegavam até Timor para o comprar. O comércio trouxe riqueza aos reinos, mas também conflitos, e no século XIX as matas de sândalo tinham diminuído muito.
summary.id: Selama berabad-abad Timor terkenal karena cendana putih, kayu harum yang sangat dicari di Tiongkok, India dan tempat lain. Pedagang Tiongkok, Jawa, Melayu dan kemudian Eropa berlayar ke Timor untuk membelinya. Perdagangan ini membawa kekayaan bagi kerajaan, tetapi juga konflik, dan pada abad ke-19 hutan cendana sudah sangat berkurang.
summary.en: For centuries Timor was famous for white sandalwood, a fragrant wood wanted in China, India and beyond. Chinese, Javanese, Malay and later European traders sailed to Timor to buy it. The trade brought wealth to kingdoms but also conflict, and by the 19th century the sandalwood forests had shrunk greatly.

text.tet: Ai-kameli mutin (Santalum album) mak ai ki'ik ida. Ninia ai-isin no ninia mina morin di'ak durante tinan barak. Ema sunu ai-kameli hanesan insensu iha templu, uza iha perfume no ai-moruk, no ko'a ba kaixa no estátua. Ai ne'e moris neineik, no presiza ai-horis seluk besik nia, tanba ninia abut foti hahán balu husi ai-horis viziñu nia abut. Uluk Timór no illa sira besik iha ai-kameli fuik barak. Tan ne'e, durante sékulu barak, naran 'Timór' liga ho ai-kameli iha livru Ázia no Europa nian.
text.pt: O sândalo branco (Santalum album), em tétum ai-kameli, é uma pequena árvore cujo cerne e óleo conservam um cheiro doce durante muitos anos. Era queimado como incenso nos templos, usado em perfumes e medicamentos e esculpido em caixas e estátuas. A árvore cresce devagar e precisa de outras plantas por perto, porque as suas raízes tiram parte do alimento das raízes das plantas vizinhas. Timor e as ilhas próximas tinham outrora grandes matas de sândalo. Por isso, durante séculos, o nome 'Timor' andou ligado ao sândalo nos escritos asiáticos e europeus.
text.id: Cendana putih (Santalum album), dalam bahasa Tetun ai-kameli, adalah pohon kecil yang kayu teras dan minyaknya tetap harum selama bertahun-tahun. Orang membakarnya sebagai dupa di kuil, memakainya untuk parfum dan obat, serta mengukirnya menjadi kotak dan patung. Pohon ini tumbuh lambat dan membutuhkan tanaman lain di dekatnya, karena akarnya mengambil sebagian makanan dari akar tanaman tetangganya. Dahulu Timor dan pulau-pulau di sekitarnya memiliki banyak hutan cendana liar. Karena itu, selama berabad-abad nama 'Timor' dikaitkan dengan cendana dalam tulisan-tulisan Asia dan Eropa.
text.en: White sandalwood (Santalum album), called ai-kameli in Tetun, is a small tree whose heartwood and oil keep a sweet smell for many years. People burned it as incense in temples, used it in perfumes and medicines and carved it into boxes and statues. The tree grows slowly and needs other plants nearby, because its roots take part of their food from the roots of neighbouring plants. Timor and nearby islands once had large wild stands of sandalwood. For this reason, for centuries the name 'Timor' was linked to sandalwood in Asian and European writings.

heading.tet: Rejistu tuan husi Xina no Java
heading.pt: Registos antigos da China e de Java
heading.id: Catatan lama dari Tiongkok dan Jawa
heading.en: Old records from China and Java

text.tet: Livru Xina sira mak rejistu hakerek tuan liu balu ne'ebé temi Timór. Livru ida husi sékulu 13, Zhu Fan Zhi, bolu illa ne'e Ti-wu no temi ninia ai-kameli. Maizumenus tinan 1350, viajante Wang Dayuan hakerek katak iha Timór nia foho sira ai-kameli moris, no ema troka ho osan-mutin, besi, kopu no hena kór oioin. Iha Java, poema Nagarakretagama (1365) temi Timór iha rai sira ne'ebé liga ho reinu Majapahit. Ró-na'in Java no Malaiu lori ai-kameli ba portu seluk iha loro-monu, no husi ne'ebá ai ne'e to'o Índia no fatin dook seluk.
text.pt: Os livros chineses estão entre os registos escritos mais antigos que falam de Timor. Uma obra do século XIII, o Zhu Fan Zhi, chama à ilha Ti-wu e refere o seu sândalo. Por volta de 1350, o viajante Wang Dayuan escreveu que nas montanhas de Timor crescia sândalo, trocado por prata, ferro, taças e panos coloridos. Em Java, o poema da corte Nagarakretagama (1365) inclui Timor entre as terras ligadas ao reino de Majapahit. Navegadores javaneses e malaios levavam a madeira para portos a oeste, e dali ela chegava à Índia e mais longe.
text.id: Buku-buku Tiongkok termasuk catatan tertulis tertua yang menyebut Timor. Sebuah karya abad ke-13, Zhu Fan Zhi, menyebut pulau ini Ti-wu dan mencatat cendananya. Sekitar tahun 1350, pengelana Wang Dayuan menulis bahwa di pegunungan Timor tumbuh cendana, yang ditukar dengan perak, besi, cawan dan kain berwarna. Di Jawa, syair istana Nagarakretagama (1365) mencantumkan Timor di antara daerah yang terkait dengan Kerajaan Majapahit. Pelaut Jawa dan Melayu membawa kayu ini ke pelabuhan-pelabuhan di barat, dan dari sana cendana sampai ke India dan tempat yang lebih jauh.
text.en: Chinese books are among the oldest written records that mention Timor. A 13th-century work, the Zhu Fan Zhi, calls the island Ti-wu and notes its sandalwood. Around 1350 the traveller Wang Dayuan wrote that sandalwood grew in Timor's mountains and was exchanged for silver, iron, cups and coloured cloth. In Java, the court poem Nagarakretagama (1365) lists Timor among the lands linked to the Majapahit kingdom. Javanese and Malay sailors carried the wood to ports in the west, and from there it reached India and lands further away.

text.tet: Bainhira Portugés sira okupa Malaka iha 1511, eskritór Portugés Tomé Pires hakerek buat ne'ebé komersiante Malaiu sira dehan: Maromak kria Timór ba ai-kameli. Ró Portugés sira hahú vizita illa ne'e atu buka ai-kameli maizumenus iha 1515. Iha 1522, ema sira ne'ebé moris hela husi Magalhães nia viajen para iha Timór, no haree komersiante husi Luzon (Filipinas) sosa ai-kameli ho osan-mean. Depois Portugés sira harii Makau iha dékada 1550, sira lori ai-kameli ba ne'ebá no ba Xina. Depois, komersiante husi Makasar (Sulawesi) no Kompañia Olandeza Índia Orientál mós mai buka negósiu ne'e. Kompetisaun ba ai-kameli lori funu iha illa.
text.pt: Depois de os portugueses tomarem Malaca, em 1511, o escritor português Tomé Pires registou um dito dos mercadores malaios: Deus fez Timor para o sândalo. Os navios portugueses começaram a visitar a ilha à procura de sândalo por volta de 1515. Em 1522, os sobreviventes da viagem de Fernão de Magalhães pararam em Timor e viram mercadores de Luzon, nas Filipinas, a comprar sândalo com ouro. Depois da fundação de Macau, nos anos 1550, os portugueses levavam sândalo para lá e para a China. Mais tarde, mercadores de Macassar, em Sulawesi, e a Companhia Holandesa das Índias Orientais disputaram este comércio, e a rivalidade provocou guerras na ilha.
text.id: Setelah Portugis merebut Malaka pada 1511, penulis Portugis Tomé Pires mencatat ungkapan para pedagang Melayu: Tuhan menciptakan Timor untuk cendana. Kapal-kapal Portugis mulai mengunjungi pulau ini untuk mencari cendana sekitar tahun 1515. Pada 1522, para penyintas pelayaran Magelhaens singgah di Timor dan melihat pedagang dari Luzon, Filipina, membeli cendana dengan emas. Setelah Makau didirikan pada tahun 1550-an, Portugis membawa cendana ke sana dan ke Tiongkok. Kemudian pedagang dari Makassar di Sulawesi dan Kongsi Dagang Hindia Timur Belanda (VOC) ikut bersaing, dan persaingan memperebutkan cendana memicu perang di pulau itu.
text.en: After the Portuguese took Malacca in 1511, the Portuguese writer Tomé Pires recorded a saying of Malay traders: God made Timor for sandalwood. Portuguese ships began to visit the island for sandalwood around 1515. In 1522 the survivors of Magellan's voyage stopped at Timor and saw merchants from Luzon, in the Philippines, buying sandalwood with gold. After Macau was founded in the 1550s, the Portuguese carried sandalwood there and on to China. Later, traders from Makassar in Sulawesi and the Dutch East India Company competed for the trade, and rivalry over sandalwood led to wars on the island.

heading.tet: Riku-soin, funu no ai-kameli nia ramata
heading.pt: Riqueza, conflito e o fim das matas de sândalo
heading.id: Kekayaan, konflik dan berakhirnya hutan cendana
heading.en: Wealth, conflict and the end of the sandalwood forests

text.tet: Ai-kameli fó riku-soin no podér ba liurai sira ne'ebé kontrola ai-laran no tasi-ibun, fatin ne'ebé ró sira tula ai. Maibé negósiu ne'e mós halo reinu sira kompete no funu malu, no ajuda fahe illa. Ema ko'a ai lalais liu duké ai bele moris fali. Iha sékulu 19, ai-kameli fuik sira sai menus tebes ona. Istoriadór sira dehan katak negósiu ne'e la husik servisu ka indústria barak iha illa. Depois, kafé sai esportasaun prinsipál. Ohin loron ai-kameli fuik raru iha Timór-Leste. Kuda no proteje ai foun ajuda rai patrimóniu ida-ne'e ba jerasaun aban-bainrua.
text.pt: O sândalo deu riqueza e poder aos liurais que controlavam as matas e as praias onde os navios carregavam a madeira. Mas o comércio também criou rivalidades entre reinos e ajudou a dividir a ilha. As árvores eram cortadas mais depressa do que conseguiam voltar a crescer e, no século XIX, as antigas matas de sândalo tinham diminuído muito. Os historiadores notam que este comércio deixou poucos empregos ou indústrias duradouros na ilha. O café tornou-se então o principal produto de exportação. Hoje, o sândalo selvagem é raro em Timor-Leste, e plantar e proteger novas árvores ajuda a manter vivo este património.
text.id: Cendana memberi kekayaan dan kekuasaan kepada para liurai yang menguasai hutan dan pantai tempat kapal memuat kayu. Namun perdagangan ini juga menimbulkan persaingan antarkerajaan dan ikut memecah belah pulau. Pohon ditebang lebih cepat daripada kemampuannya tumbuh kembali, dan pada abad ke-19 hutan cendana lama sudah sangat berkurang. Sejarawan mencatat bahwa perdagangan ini hanya meninggalkan sedikit lapangan kerja atau industri yang bertahan di pulau itu. Kopi kemudian menjadi ekspor utama. Kini cendana liar jarang ditemukan di Timor-Leste, dan menanam serta melindungi pohon baru membantu menjaga warisan ini.
text.en: Sandalwood gave wealth and power to the liurai who controlled the forests and the beaches where ships loaded the wood. But the trade also made kingdoms compete and fight, and it helped to divide the island. Trees were cut faster than they could grow back, and by the 19th century the old sandalwood forests had shrunk greatly. Historians note that the trade left few lasting jobs or industries on the island. Coffee then became the main export. Today wild sandalwood is rare in Timor-Leste, and planting and protecting new trees helps keep this heritage alive.

summary.tet: Komersiante Portugés sira to'o Timór iha sékulu 16 nia hahú atu buka ai-kameli; fonte barak temi tinan 1515 no tasi-ibun Lifau, iha Oe-Kusi. Frade dominikanu sira hahú sira-nia misaun iha rejiaun ne'e iha 1556, husi illa Solor. Durante tempu naruk Portugés sira uitoan de'it, no sira depende ba aliansa ho reinu lokál sira.
summary.pt: Os mercadores portugueses chegaram a Timor no início do século XVI, à procura de sândalo; muitas fontes indicam 1515 e a praia de Lifau, em Oé-Cusse. Os frades dominicanos começaram a missão na região em 1556, a partir da ilha de Solor. Durante muito tempo os portugueses foram poucos e dependiam de alianças com os reinos locais.
summary.id: Pedagang Portugis tiba di Timor pada awal abad ke-16 untuk mencari cendana; banyak sumber menyebut tahun 1515 dan pantai Lifau di Oé-Cusse. Biarawan Dominikan memulai misi di wilayah ini pada 1556 dari Pulau Solor. Lama sekali orang Portugis hanya sedikit dan bergantung pada persekutuan dengan kerajaan setempat.
summary.en: Portuguese traders reached Timor in the early 1500s, looking for sandalwood; many sources give 1515 and the beach of Lifau, in Oecusse. Dominican friars began their mission in the region in 1556 from the island of Solor. For a long time the Portuguese were few, and they depended on alliances with local kingdoms.

text.tet: Iha 1511 Portugés sira okupa Malaka, portu negósiu boot iha Penínsulu Malaiu. Husi ne'ebá sira rona kona-ba illa sira ne'ebé iha ai-kameli no produtu folin-boot seluk. Timór mosu iha mapa Portugés ida iha 1512, no ró Portugés sira mai sosa ai-kameli depois ne'e. Fonte barak dehan katak sira tun dahuluk iha 1515 iha Lifau, iha Oe-Kusi nia tasi-ibun norte. Maibé tinan loloos la klaru: fonte sira temi tinan entre 1512 no 1515. Vizitante dahuluk sira mak komersiante, la'ós ukun-na'in. Sira hela fulan hirak, tula ai-kameli, no fila ho anin monsaun.
text.pt: Em 1511 os portugueses conquistaram Malaca, o grande porto comercial da Península Malaia. Dali souberam das ilhas que produziam especiarias e sândalo. Timor aparece num mapa português em 1512, e pouco depois navios portugueses vieram comprar sândalo. Muitas fontes datam o primeiro desembarque de 1515, em Lifau, na costa norte do atual Oé-Cusse, mas o ano exato é incerto: as datas indicadas vão de 1512 a 1515. Os primeiros visitantes eram mercadores, não governantes. Ficavam alguns meses, carregavam sândalo e partiam com os ventos da monção.
text.id: Pada 1511 Portugis merebut Malaka, pelabuhan dagang besar di Semenanjung Melayu. Dari sana mereka mendengar tentang pulau-pulau penghasil rempah dan cendana. Timor muncul di peta Portugis pada 1512, dan tak lama kemudian kapal-kapal Portugis datang membeli cendana. Banyak sumber menyebut pendaratan pertama terjadi pada 1515 di Lifau, di pantai utara Oé-Cusse sekarang, tetapi tahun pastinya tidak jelas: tanggal yang disebut berkisar antara 1512 dan 1515. Para pengunjung pertama adalah pedagang, bukan penguasa. Mereka tinggal beberapa bulan, memuat cendana, lalu berlayar pulang mengikuti angin muson.
text.en: In 1511 the Portuguese captured Malacca, the great trading port on the Malay Peninsula. From there they learned about the islands that produced spices and sandalwood. Timor appeared on a Portuguese map in 1512, and Portuguese ships soon came to buy sandalwood. Many sources date the first landing to 1515 at Lifau, on the north coast of today's Oecusse, but the exact year is uncertain: dates from 1512 to 1515 are given. The first visitors were traders, not rulers. They stayed a few months, loaded sandalwood and sailed away with the monsoon winds.

text.tet: Misionáriu katóliku sira tuir komersiante sira. Iha 1556, frade dominikanu balu hahú servisu iha rejiaun ne'e, ho baze iha illa Solor, iha Timór nia norte. Iha dékada 1560 sira harii forte ida iha Solor atu proteje sira-nia misaun no knua kristaun sira. Husi Solor, no depois husi Larantuka iha illa Flores, frade sira bá Timór, batiza liurai balu no sira-nia família, no harii kapela ki'ik sira. Iha 1585, vise-rei Portugés iha Goa (Índia) tau Solor iha ninia ukun okos. Maski nune'e, durante tempu naruk Timór-oan barak liu kaer metin sira-nia fiar rasik.
text.pt: Os missionários católicos seguiram os mercadores. Em 1556, um grupo de frades dominicanos começou a trabalhar na região, a partir da ilha de Solor, a norte de Timor. Nos anos 1560, construíram um forte em Solor para proteger a missão e as aldeias cristãs vizinhas. De Solor e, mais tarde, de Larantuka, na ilha das Flores, os frades iam a Timor, batizavam alguns governantes e as suas famílias e construíam pequenas igrejas. Em 1585, o vice-rei português em Goa, na Índia, colocou Solor sob a sua autoridade. Mesmo assim, durante muito tempo a maioria dos timorenses manteve as suas crenças.
text.id: Para misionaris Katolik menyusul para pedagang. Pada 1556 sekelompok biarawan Dominikan mulai berkarya di wilayah ini dengan pangkalan di Pulau Solor, di utara Timor. Pada tahun 1560-an mereka membangun benteng di Solor untuk melindungi misi dan kampung-kampung Kristen di sekitarnya. Dari Solor, dan kemudian dari Larantuka di Pulau Flores, para biarawan pergi ke Timor, membaptis beberapa penguasa beserta keluarganya, dan membangun gereja-gereja kecil. Pada 1585 raja muda Portugis di Goa, India, menempatkan Solor di bawah kekuasaannya. Meski begitu, lama sekali sebagian besar orang Timor tetap memegang kepercayaan mereka sendiri.
text.en: Catholic missionaries followed the traders. In 1556 a group of Dominican friars began working in the region, based on the island of Solor, north of Timor. In the 1560s they built a fort on Solor to protect their mission and the Christian villages around it. From Solor, and later from Larantuka on the island of Flores, the friars travelled to Timor, baptised some rulers and their families, and built small chapels. In 1585 the Portuguese viceroy in Goa, India, placed Solor under his authority. Even so, for a long time most Timorese kept their own beliefs.

heading.tet: Lifau: Portugés nia baze dahuluk iha Timór
heading.pt: Lifau: a primeira base portuguesa em Timor
heading.id: Lifau: pangkalan Portugis pertama di Timor
heading.en: Lifau: the first Portuguese base on Timor

text.tet: Lifau, portu ai-kameli ki'ik ida iha Oe-Kusi nia tasi-ibun, sai Portugés nia sentru prinsipál iha Timór. Frade dominikanu sira hela iha ne'ebá, no komersiante kristaun ho raan Portugés no lokál kahur, ne'ebé depois ema bolu Topasse, halo Lifau sai sira-nia baze. Iha 1702, governadór dahuluk ne'ebé Portugál haruka hahú ninia knaar iha Lifau, no sira harii forte ida naran Santo António. Lifau sai sentru Portugés nian to'o 1769, bainhira Topasse sira-nia atake obriga governadór atu muda kapitál ba Dili. Oe-Kusi hela nafatin iha Portugés nia liman, no ohin loron sei parte husi Timór-Leste.
text.pt: Lifau, um pequeno porto de sândalo na costa de Oé-Cusse, tornou-se o principal centro português em Timor. Ali se instalaram frades dominicanos, e mercadores cristãos de ascendência portuguesa e local misturada, mais tarde chamados topasses, fizeram dele a sua base. Em 1702, o primeiro governador enviado por Portugal assumiu funções em Lifau, onde se construiu o forte de Santo António. Lifau foi o centro da presença portuguesa até 1769, quando os ataques dos topasses levaram o governador a mudar a capital para Díli. Oé-Cusse continuou português e ainda hoje faz parte de Timor-Leste.
text.id: Lifau, pelabuhan cendana kecil di pantai Oé-Cusse, menjadi pusat utama Portugis di Timor. Biarawan Dominikan menetap di sana, dan pedagang Kristen berdarah campuran Portugis dan lokal, yang kemudian disebut Topas, menjadikannya pangkalan. Pada 1702 gubernur pertama yang dikirim Portugal mulai bertugas di Lifau, dan di sana dibangun benteng Santo António. Lifau tetap menjadi pusat kegiatan Portugis sampai 1769, ketika serangan kaum Topas memaksa gubernur memindahkan ibu kota ke Dili. Oé-Cusse tetap milik Portugis dan sampai sekarang menjadi bagian dari Timor-Leste.
text.en: Lifau, a small sandalwood port on the coast of Oecusse, became the main Portuguese centre on Timor. Dominican friars settled there, and Christian traders of mixed Portuguese and local descent, later called Topasses, made it their base. In 1702 the first governor sent by Portugal took office at Lifau, where a fort named Santo António was built. Lifau remained the centre of Portuguese activity until 1769, when attacks by the Topasses forced the governor to move the capital to Dili. Oecusse stayed Portuguese and is still part of Timor-Leste today.

text.tet: Iha 2015 Timór-Leste komemora tinan 500 interasaun ho Portugál, hamutuk ho aniversáriu ba dala-40 Proklamasaun Independénsia. Iha 27 Novembru 2015 sira inaugura monumentu ida iha Lifau: karavela bronze ida, ró-vela Portugés nian, ho naruk maizumenus metru 13, ho estátua bronze ró-na'in, padre no Timór-oan sira. Nia hamriik besik padraun (marku fatuk) tuan ida husi 1974. Monumentu ne'e hanoin fali istória naruk no komplikadu ida: negósiu no fiar, maibé mós ukun koloniál. Ohin loron Portugés mak lian ofisiál ida, no Timór-Leste mak membru Komunidade Nasaun sira ne'ebé ko'alia Portugés (CPLP).
text.pt: Em 2015, Timor-Leste assinalou os 500 anos de interação com Portugal, juntamente com o 40.º aniversário da Proclamação da Independência. A 27 de novembro de 2015 foi inaugurado em Lifau um monumento: uma caravela de bronze, navio à vela português, com cerca de 13 metros, com figuras de bronze de marinheiros, de um padre e de timorenses. Fica perto de um padrão mais antigo, de 1974. O monumento lembra uma história longa e complexa: comércio e fé, mas também domínio colonial. Hoje o português é uma das línguas oficiais e Timor-Leste é membro da Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa (CPLP).
text.id: Pada 2015 Timor-Leste memperingati 500 tahun interaksi dengan Portugal, bersamaan dengan ulang tahun ke-40 Proklamasi Kemerdekaan. Pada 27 November 2015 sebuah monumen diresmikan di Lifau: kapal karavel Portugis dari perunggu sepanjang sekitar 13 meter, dengan patung perunggu pelaut, seorang pastor dan orang Timor. Monumen ini berdiri di dekat tugu batu (padrão) yang lebih tua dari tahun 1974. Monumen itu mengingatkan sejarah yang panjang dan rumit: perdagangan dan iman, tetapi juga penjajahan. Kini bahasa Portugis menjadi salah satu bahasa resmi, dan Timor-Leste adalah anggota Komunitas Negara-Negara Berbahasa Portugis (CPLP).
text.en: In 2015 Timor-Leste marked 500 years of contact with Portugal, together with the 40th anniversary of the Proclamation of Independence. On 27 November 2015 a monument was opened at Lifau: a bronze caravel, a Portuguese sailing ship, about 13 metres long, with bronze figures of sailors, a priest and Timorese people. It stands near an older stone marker (padrão) from 1974. The monument recalls a long and complex story: trade and faith, but also colonial rule. Today Portuguese is an official language, and Timor-Leste is a member of the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP).

title.tet: Topasse sira no sékulu 17–18
title.pt: Os topasses e os séculos XVII–XVIII
title.en: The Topasses and the 17th–18th centuries

summary.tet: Topasse sira mak povu katóliku ho raan kahur ne'ebé ko'alia Portugés, no moris iha Portugés nia baze iha Solor no Larantuka. Família Hornay no da Costa lidera sira, no durante sékulu ida maizumenus sira kontrola negósiu ai-kameli barak. Sira funu hasoru Olanda, no dala ruma hasoru governadór Portugés sira mós.
summary.pt: Os topasses eram um povo católico, de língua portuguesa e ascendência mista, nascido em torno das bases portuguesas de Solor e Larantuka. Chefiados pelas famílias rivais Hornay e da Costa, controlaram grande parte do comércio do sândalo durante cerca de um século. Combateram os holandeses e, por vezes, até os governadores portugueses.
summary.id: Kaum Topas adalah orang Katolik berdarah campuran yang berbahasa Portugis dan tumbuh di sekitar pangkalan Portugis di Solor dan Larantuka. Dipimpin keluarga Hornay dan da Costa yang saling bersaing, mereka menguasai sebagian besar perdagangan cendana selama sekitar satu abad. Mereka melawan Belanda dan kadang-kadang juga gubernur Portugis.
summary.en: The Topasses were a Catholic, Portuguese-speaking people of mixed descent who grew up around the Portuguese bases of Solor and Larantuka. Led by the rival Hornay and da Costa families, they controlled much of the sandalwood trade for about a century. They fought the Dutch and sometimes even the Portuguese governors.

text.tet: Hahú iha dékada 1560, komunidade kahur ida moris iha Portugés nia forte iha Solor nia sorin: soldadu, ró-na'in no komersiante Portugés, sira-nia feen husi Solor, Flores no Timór, no sira-nia oan sira. Sira mak katóliku, no ko'alia Portugés no lian lokál. Bainhira Kompañia Olandeza Índia Orientál okupa Solor iha 1613, sira barak muda ba Larantuka, iha Flores, no sira bolu an 'Larantuqueiros'. Olanda sira bolu sira 'Portugés metan'. Naran 'Topasse' karik mai husi liafuan ida ne'ebé ema uza iha Índia, maibé ninia orijen sei la klaru. Ho tempu, sira simu mós ema lokál no aliadu barak.
text.pt: A partir dos anos 1560, formou-se uma comunidade mista em torno do forte português de Solor: soldados, marinheiros e mercadores portugueses, as suas mulheres de Solor, das Flores e de Timor, e os seus filhos. Eram católicos e falavam português e línguas locais. Quando a Companhia Holandesa das Índias Orientais tomou Solor, em 1613, muitos mudaram-se para Larantuka, nas Flores, e chamavam-se a si próprios larantuqueiros. Os holandeses chamavam-lhes 'portugueses negros'. O nome topasses vem provavelmente de uma palavra usada na Índia, mas a sua origem é discutida. Com o tempo, acolheram também muitos habitantes locais e aliados.
text.id: Sejak tahun 1560-an, sebuah komunitas campuran tumbuh di sekitar benteng Portugis di Solor: prajurit, pelaut dan pedagang Portugis, istri-istri mereka dari Solor, Flores dan Timor, serta anak-anak mereka. Mereka beragama Katolik dan berbicara bahasa Portugis serta bahasa setempat. Ketika VOC merebut Solor pada 1613, banyak dari mereka pindah ke Larantuka di Flores, dan mereka menyebut diri Larantuqueiros. Orang Belanda menyebut mereka 'Portugis Hitam'. Nama Topas mungkin berasal dari sebuah kata yang dipakai di India, tetapi asal-usulnya masih diperdebatkan. Lama-kelamaan mereka juga menerima banyak penduduk setempat dan sekutu.
text.en: From the 1560s a mixed community grew up around the Portuguese fort on Solor: Portuguese soldiers, sailors and traders, their wives from Solor, Flores and Timor, and their children. They were Catholic and spoke Portuguese and local languages. When the Dutch East India Company took Solor in 1613, many of them moved to Larantuka, on Flores, and they called themselves Larantuqueiros. The Dutch called them 'Black Portuguese'. The name Topasses probably comes from a word used in India, but its origin is debated. Over time they also took in many local people and allies.

heading.pt: As famílias Hornay e da Costa
heading.en: The Hornay and da Costa families

text.tet: Família rua mak lidera Topasse sira. Família Hornay hahú ho Jan de Hornay, ema Olanda ida ne'ebé husik Olanda nia servisu no tama Portugés nia parte iha sékulu 17. Ninia oan António Hornay sai lider ida ne'ebé iha podér boot. Família da Costa, ho lider hanesan Mateus da Costa no depois Gaspar da Costa, mak sira-nia rivál boot. Durante tinan barak família rua ne'e funu malu ho raan atu kaer podér, maibé ikus mai sira fahe podér. Sira-nia lider dala barak iha títulu 'kapitaun-mór' (kapitaun boot), no liurai barak tenke halo tuir sira.
text.pt: Duas famílias chefiavam os topasses. A família Hornay começou com Jan de Hornay, um holandês que deixou o serviço holandês e passou para o lado português no século XVII; o seu filho António Hornay tornou-se um chefe poderoso. A família da Costa, com chefes como Mateus da Costa e, mais tarde, Gaspar da Costa, era a grande rival. Durante muitos anos, as duas famílias travaram uma luta sangrenta pelo poder, mas acabaram por partilhá-lo. Os seus chefes usavam muitas vezes o título de capitão-mor, e muitos governantes timorenses tinham de lhes obedecer.
text.id: Dua keluarga memimpin kaum Topas. Keluarga Hornay berawal dari Jan de Hornay, seorang Belanda yang meninggalkan dinas Belanda dan berpihak kepada Portugis pada abad ke-17; putranya, António Hornay, menjadi pemimpin yang berkuasa. Keluarga da Costa, dengan pemimpin seperti Mateus da Costa dan kemudian Gaspar da Costa, adalah saingan besarnya. Selama bertahun-tahun kedua keluarga itu bertarung secara berdarah memperebutkan kekuasaan, tetapi akhirnya berbagi kekuasaan. Pemimpin mereka sering bergelar capitão-mor (kapten utama), dan banyak penguasa Timor harus tunduk kepada mereka.
text.en: Two families led the Topasses. The Hornay family began with Jan de Hornay, a Dutchman who left Dutch service and joined the Portuguese side in the 17th century; his son António Hornay became a powerful leader. The da Costa family, with leaders such as Mateus da Costa and later Gaspar da Costa, was their great rival. For many years the two families fought a bloody struggle for power, but in the end they shared it. Their leaders often held the title of capitão-mor (chief captain), and many Timorese rulers had to obey them.

text.tet: Iha sékulu 17 no 18, Topasse sira sai podér boot liu iha Timór. Sira iha kilat, no ida-ne'e ajuda sira ukun reinu barak, liuliu iha illa nia parte loro-monu. Sira obriga liurai sira atu lori ai-kameli ba tasi-ibun, no sira mak determina folin. Sira fa'an ai ne'e ba komersiante husi Makau ka ba Olanda. Lifau, iha Oe-Kusi, sai sira-nia baze prinsipál ida. Topasse sira dala barak la rona governadór ne'ebé mai husi Goa ka Makau. Bainhira Portugál nia Rei koko ukun Timór direta, sira serka Portugés sira, no iha 1769 Portugés sira husik Lifau no muda ba Dili.
text.pt: Nos séculos XVII e XVIII, os topasses tornaram-se a maior força de Timor. Tinham armas de fogo, o que os ajudou a dominar muitos reinos, sobretudo no oeste da ilha. Obrigavam os governantes timorenses a levar o sândalo até à costa e controlavam o seu preço; a madeira era vendida a mercadores de Macau ou aos holandeses. Lifau, em Oé-Cusse, tornou-se uma das suas principais bases. Os topasses ignoravam muitas vezes os governadores enviados de Goa ou de Macau: quando o rei de Portugal tentou governar Timor diretamente, cercaram os portugueses, que em 1769 deixaram Lifau e foram para Díli.
text.id: Pada abad ke-17 dan ke-18, kaum Topas menjadi kekuatan terbesar di Timor. Mereka memiliki senapan, sehingga dapat menguasai banyak kerajaan, terutama di bagian barat pulau. Mereka memaksa para penguasa Timor membawa cendana ke pantai dan mengendalikan harganya; kayu itu dijual kepada pedagang dari Makau atau kepada Belanda. Lifau di Oé-Cusse menjadi salah satu pangkalan utama mereka. Kaum Topas sering mengabaikan gubernur yang dikirim dari Goa atau Makau: ketika raja Portugal mencoba memerintah Timor secara langsung, mereka mengepung orang Portugis, yang pada 1769 meninggalkan Lifau dan pindah ke Dili.
text.en: In the 17th and 18th centuries the Topasses became the strongest power on Timor. They had muskets, which helped them dominate many kingdoms, especially in the west of the island. They pressed Timorese rulers to bring sandalwood to the coast and controlled its price; the wood was sold to merchants from Macau or to the Dutch. Lifau, in Oecusse, became one of their main bases. The Topasses often ignored the governors sent from Goa or Macau: when the king of Portugal tried to rule Timor directly, they besieged the Portuguese, who in 1769 left Lifau for Dili.

heading.tet: Funu ho Olanda no funu Penfui
heading.pt: A guerra com os holandeses e a batalha de Penfui
heading.id: Perang dengan Belanda dan pertempuran Penfui
heading.en: War with the Dutch and the battle of Penfui

text.tet: Iha dékada 1650, Kompañia Olandeza Índia Orientál (VOC) harii baze ida iha Kupang, iha Timór nia rohan loro-monu, no halo aliansa ho reinu lokál sira iha ne'ebá. Topasse no Olanda funu malu durante sékulu ida maizumenus atu kontrola illa no ninia negósiu. Iha 1748 reinu balu iha Timór loro-monu hasoru lider Topasse Gaspar da Costa. Iha 9 Novembru 1749, iha Penfui besik Kupang, forsa VOC ne'ebé ki'ik liu manan hasoru Topasse nia tropa boot, depois sira-nia aliadu Timór-oan husik funu-fatin. Gaspar da Costa mate. Depois ne'e Topasse sira-nia podér tun, maibé sira kaer metin nafatin Oe-Kusi.
text.pt: Nos anos 1650, a Companhia Holandesa das Índias Orientais (VOC) instalou uma base em Kupang, no extremo oeste de Timor, e aliou-se aos reinos locais. Topasses e holandeses disputaram a ilha e o seu comércio durante cerca de um século. Em 1748, vários reinos de Timor Ocidental revoltaram-se contra o chefe topasse Gaspar da Costa. A 9 de novembro de 1749, em Penfui, perto de Kupang, um grande exército topasse foi derrotado por uma força holandesa mais pequena, depois de os seus aliados timorenses abandonarem o campo, e Gaspar da Costa morreu. A partir daí, o poder topasse diminuiu, mas manteve-se em Oé-Cusse.
text.id: Pada tahun 1650-an, VOC mendirikan pangkalan di Kupang, di ujung barat Timor, dan bersekutu dengan kerajaan-kerajaan setempat. Kaum Topas dan Belanda bersaing menguasai pulau dan perdagangannya selama sekitar satu abad. Pada 1748 beberapa kerajaan di Timor Barat berbalik melawan pemimpin Topas, Gaspar da Costa. Pada 9 November 1749, di Penfui dekat Kupang, pasukan besar Topas dikalahkan oleh pasukan VOC yang lebih kecil setelah sekutu Timor mereka meninggalkan medan perang, dan Gaspar da Costa tewas. Setelah itu kekuasaan Topas merosot, tetapi mereka tetap bertahan di Oé-Cusse.
text.en: In the 1650s the Dutch East India Company (VOC) set up a base at Kupang, at the western end of Timor, and allied with local kingdoms there. The Topasses and the Dutch fought for control of the island and its trade for about a century. In 1748 several kingdoms of West Timor turned against the Topass leader Gaspar da Costa. On 9 November 1749, at Penfui near Kupang, a large Topass army was defeated by a smaller VOC force after its Timorese allies left the field, and Gaspar da Costa was killed. After this, Topass power declined, but they held on in Oecusse.

title.tet: Husi Lifau ba Dili (1702–1769)
title.pt: De Lifau a Díli (1702–1769)
title.en: From Lifau to Dili (1702–1769)

summary.tet: Iha 1702 Portugál haruka ninia governadór dahuluk ba Timór, no nia hatuur ninia sede iha Lifau, iha Oe-Kusi. Durante tinan besik 70, governadór sira iha ne'ebá funu hasoru Topasse no reinu sira ne'ebé revolta. Iha 1769, bainhira inimigu serka Lifau, Governadór Teles de Meneses sai no harii kapitál foun iha Dili.
summary.pt: Em 1702 Portugal enviou o primeiro governador para Timor, que se instalou em Lifau, em Oé-Cusse. Durante quase setenta anos, os governadores lutaram ali contra os topasses e contra reinos revoltados. Em 1769, com Lifau cercada, o governador Teles de Meneses partiu e fundou uma nova capital em Díli.
summary.id: Pada 1702 Portugal mengirim gubernur pertamanya ke Timor, yang berkedudukan di Lifau, Oé-Cusse. Selama hampir tujuh puluh tahun para gubernur di sana berjuang melawan kaum Topas dan kerajaan yang memberontak. Pada 1769, ketika Lifau dikepung, Gubernur Teles de Meneses pergi dan mendirikan ibu kota baru di Dili.
summary.en: In 1702 Portugal sent its first governor to Timor, who set up his seat at Lifau, in Oecusse. For almost seventy years the governors there struggled with the Topasses and with rebellious kingdoms. In 1769, with Lifau under siege, Governor Teles de Meneses left and founded a new capital at Dili.

text.tet: Maizumenus tinan 1700, Portugál hakarak kontrola liu Timór no ninia ai-kameli. Iha 1702, António Coelho Guerreiro to'o hanesan governadór no kapitaun-jenerál dahuluk ba Timór no Solor. Nia hatuur ninia sede iha Lifau, iha Oe-Kusi nia tasi-ibun, no sira harii forte Santo António iha ne'ebá. Lifau ki'ik: ema deskreve nia hanesan knua ida ho uma '40 ka 50'. Topasse sira, ne'ebé hatene ona ukun tuir sira-nia hakarak rasik, la hakarak governadór. Sira-nia lider Domingos da Costa koko hapara Guerreiro, no tinan hirak depois Topasse sira duni sai nia.
text.pt: Por volta de 1700, Portugal queria controlar melhor Timor e o seu sândalo. Em 1702 chegou António Coelho Guerreiro, primeiro governador e capitão-general de Timor e Solor. Instalou a sua sede em Lifau, na costa de Oé-Cusse, onde se construiu o forte de Santo António. Lifau era pequena: foi descrita como uma povoação de '40 ou 50 casas'. Os topasses, habituados a mandar à sua maneira, não queriam um governador. O seu chefe, Domingos da Costa, tentou impedir a instalação de Guerreiro e, poucos anos depois, os topasses expulsaram-no.
text.id: Sekitar tahun 1700, Portugal ingin lebih menguasai Timor dan cendananya. Pada 1702 António Coelho Guerreiro tiba sebagai gubernur dan kapten jenderal pertama Timor dan Solor. Ia berkedudukan di Lifau, di pantai Oé-Cusse, tempat dibangun benteng Santo António. Lifau adalah tempat kecil: pernah digambarkan sebagai permukiman dengan '40 atau 50 rumah'. Kaum Topas, yang terbiasa berkuasa menurut kehendak sendiri, tidak menginginkan gubernur. Pemimpin mereka, Domingos da Costa, berusaha menghalangi Guerreiro, dan beberapa tahun kemudian kaum Topas mengusirnya.
text.en: Around 1700, Portugal wanted more control over Timor and its sandalwood. In 1702 António Coelho Guerreiro arrived as the first governor and captain-general of Timor and Solor. He set up his seat at Lifau, on the coast of Oecusse, where the fort of Santo António was built. Lifau was small: it has been described as a settlement of '40 or 50 houses'. The Topasses, used to ruling in their own way, did not want a governor. Their leader, Domingos da Costa, tried to block Guerreiro, and a few years later the Topasses drove him out.

text.tet: Durante sékulu 18 nia parte barak, governadór sira iha Lifau iha podér uitoan de'it. Sira depende ba aliansa ne'ebé la metin ho frade dominikanu, lider Topasse no liurai sira, ne'ebé dala barak muda sira-nia parte. Governadór balu hasoru serku ka tenke halai, no reinu balu revolta hasoru Portugés. Topasse sira, ho família Hornay no da Costa, kontrola ai-kameli, no dala barak iha soldadu barak liu duké governadór. Iha tempu hanesan, Olanda husi Kupang habelar sira-nia influénsia iha loro-monu, liuliu depois funu Penfui iha 1749.
text.pt: Durante a maior parte do século XVIII, os governadores de Lifau tiveram pouco poder real. Dependiam de alianças instáveis com frades dominicanos, chefes topasses e liurais, que mudavam muitas vezes de lado. Vários governadores foram cercados ou obrigados a fugir, e alguns reinos revoltaram-se contra os portugueses. Os topasses, com as famílias Hornay e da Costa, controlavam o sândalo e tinham muitas vezes mais soldados do que o governador. Entretanto, os holandeses, a partir de Kupang, alargavam a sua influência no oeste, sobretudo depois da batalha de Penfui, em 1749.
text.id: Selama sebagian besar abad ke-18, para gubernur di Lifau hanya punya sedikit kekuasaan nyata. Mereka bergantung pada persekutuan yang goyah dengan biarawan Dominikan, pemimpin Topas dan para liurai, yang sering berganti pihak. Beberapa gubernur dikepung atau terpaksa melarikan diri, dan sejumlah kerajaan memberontak melawan Portugis. Kaum Topas, dengan keluarga Hornay dan da Costa, menguasai cendana dan sering memiliki prajurit lebih banyak daripada gubernur. Sementara itu Belanda dari Kupang memperluas pengaruhnya di barat, terutama setelah pertempuran Penfui pada 1749.
text.en: For most of the 18th century the governors at Lifau had little real power. They depended on shaky alliances with Dominican friars, Topass leaders and liurai, who often changed sides. Several governors were besieged or forced to flee, and some kingdoms rose up against the Portuguese. The Topasses, with the Hornay and da Costa families, controlled the sandalwood and often had more soldiers than the governor. Meanwhile the Dutch, from Kupang, extended their influence in the west, especially after the battle of Penfui in 1749.

text.tet: Iha 1769, forsa Topasse ne'ebé Francisco Hornay lidera serka governadór António José Teles de Meneses iha Lifau. Nia deside atu sai. Iha 11 Agostu 1769, nia estraga fatin forte ne'e, no la'o ho ró ba loro-sa'e hamutuk ho administrasaun no ema maizumenus 1 200. Uluk nia hanoin atu hela iha Vemasse, iha loro-sa'e liu, maibé ikus nia hili Dili nia baía, ne'ebé iha portu di'ak. Iha 10 Outubru 1769 servisu hahú ba kapitál foun. Oe-Kusi hela iha família Topasse sira-nia liman, no depois sai parte husi Timór Portugés.
text.pt: Em 1769, o governador António José Teles de Meneses estava cercado em Lifau por forças topasses chefiadas por Francisco Hornay. Decidiu partir. A 11 de agosto de 1769 destruiu a povoação fortificada e navegou para leste com a administração e cerca de 1200 pessoas. Pensou primeiro em instalar-se em Vemasse, mais a leste, mas escolheu a baía de Díli, que tinha um bom porto. A 10 de outubro de 1769 começaram os trabalhos da nova capital. Oé-Cusse ficou nas mãos de famílias topasses e, mais tarde, passou a fazer parte do Timor Português.
text.id: Pada 1769 Gubernur António José Teles de Meneses dikepung di Lifau oleh pasukan Topas yang dipimpin Francisco Hornay. Ia memutuskan untuk pergi. Pada 11 Agustus 1769 ia menghancurkan permukiman berbenteng itu dan berlayar ke timur bersama pemerintahannya dan sekitar 1.200 orang. Mula-mula ia berpikir untuk menetap di Vemasse, lebih ke timur, tetapi akhirnya memilih Teluk Dili yang memiliki pelabuhan yang baik. Pada 10 Oktober 1769 pembangunan ibu kota baru dimulai. Oé-Cusse tetap di tangan keluarga-keluarga Topas, dan kemudian menjadi bagian dari Timor Portugis.
text.en: In 1769 Governor António José Teles de Meneses was besieged at Lifau by Topass forces led by Francisco Hornay. He decided to leave. On 11 August 1769 he destroyed the fortified settlement and sailed east with the administration and about 1,200 people. He first thought of settling at Vemasse, further east, but chose the bay of Dili, which had a good harbour. On 10 October 1769 work began on the new capital. Oecusse stayed in the hands of Topass families and later became part of Portuguese Timor.

text.tet: Dili sai kapitál ba Portugés nia rai sira iha illa Sunda Ki'ik. Uluk, Dili mak knua ki'ik ida iha baía nia sorin. Durante sékulu rua tuir mai, nia boot neineik, ho portu, edifísiu governu nian, igreja, eskola no merkadu. Naturalista Inglés Alfred Russel Wallace vizita Dili iha 1861 no deskreve nia hanesan vila ki'ik, kiak no moras barak. Lifau lakon ninia importánsia. Ohin loron Dili mak Timór-Leste nia kapitál no sidade boot liu, no monumentu ida iha Lifau, ne'ebé sira inaugura iha 2015, hanoin fali kapitál Portugés dahuluk.
text.pt: Díli tornou-se a capital dos territórios portugueses nas Pequenas Ilhas da Sonda. No início era uma pequena povoação junto à baía. Cresceu devagar nos dois séculos seguintes, com porto, edifícios do governo, igrejas, escolas e mercados. O naturalista britânico Alfred Russel Wallace visitou Díli em 1861 e descreveu-a como uma vila pequena, pobre e pouco saudável. Lifau perdeu importância. Hoje Díli é a capital e a maior cidade de Timor-Leste, e um monumento em Lifau, inaugurado em 2015, recorda a primeira capital portuguesa.
text.id: Dili menjadi ibu kota wilayah Portugis di Kepulauan Sunda Kecil. Pada awalnya Dili hanyalah permukiman kecil di tepi teluk. Kota ini tumbuh perlahan selama dua abad berikutnya, dengan pelabuhan, gedung pemerintah, gereja, sekolah dan pasar. Naturalis Inggris Alfred Russel Wallace mengunjungi Dili pada 1861 dan menggambarkannya sebagai kota kecil yang miskin dan tidak sehat. Lifau pun kehilangan arti pentingnya. Kini Dili adalah ibu kota dan kota terbesar Timor-Leste, dan sebuah monumen di Lifau yang diresmikan pada 2015 mengenang ibu kota Portugis yang pertama.
text.en: Dili became the capital of the Portuguese territories in the Lesser Sunda Islands. At first it was a small settlement by the bay. It grew slowly over the next two centuries, with a harbour, government buildings, churches, schools and markets. The British naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace visited Dili in 1861 and described it as a small, poor and unhealthy town. Lifau lost its importance. Today Dili is the capital and largest city of Timor-Leste, and a monument at Lifau, opened in 2015, recalls the first Portuguese capital.
